items.prompt: Mr Andi says his password is always "wrong", even though he's sure it's right. The Caps Lock light is on. What is the decision?
choices: Guide the User: turn off Caps Lock and try again
Ask for his password to try it yourself
items.explanation: The device is healthy, only Caps Lock is on. Teach the user so they can solve it on their own next time.

items.prompt: Someone claiming to be a Nusa Digital technician asks for your password over the phone. What is right?
choices: Just give it, they're a technician
Refuse and be suspicious, because technicians never ask for passwords
Send it by email so it's safe
items.explanation: Technicians never ask for passwords. Anyone who asks for one should be treated as suspicious.

items.prompt: Tap the parts of the ticket that show the problem is just a simple setting.

parts.text: Complaint: the laptop makes no sound at all.
The speaker icon in the corner of the screen is on mute.
Speaker test with a tool: sound comes out normally.
The laptop has been in use for two years.

items.explanation: The speaker is proven healthy and the sound is only muted. Just guide the user to turn the sound back on.

items.prompt: Put in order how to guide a user whose monitor looks "dead" because the wrong input source is selected.
steps: Make sure the device is healthy
Explain how to pick the right input in simple words
Ask the user to try it themselves
Write the cause and fix in the ticket history
items.explanation: First make sure nothing is broken, then teach the user and let them try. The ticket note helps if the same problem comes back.

items.prompt: Mrs Rina forgot her account password. What do you do?
choices: Send her to the office's official password reset page
Make a new password and write it on paper
items.explanation: A forgotten password is solved through the official reset page. A technician doesn't need, and must not know, a user's password.
